extracted.intended_audience: national patent offices, patent attorneys/agents, applicants, and government officials involved with the Eurasian patent system
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and requirements governing grant, validity, procedure and administration of Eurasian patents under the Eurasian Patent Convention, including substantive patentability criteria, filing and examination procedures, fees, representation, and relations with national offices and the PCT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Eurasian Office shall grant a Eurasian patent for any invention that is new, involves an inventive step and is industrially applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 6 — Patent Regulations shall provide definitions of novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability and the requirement of disclosure (see Article 14(i)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of disclosure of the invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Patentability requires disclosure of the invention as prescribed by the Patent Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 14(i) — Patent Regulations will set the specific disclosure requirements; disclosure is a substantive part of patentability criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persons entitled to a Eurasian patent
rubrics_metrics.description: The right to a Eurasian patent shall belong to the inventor or his successor in title; where the inventor is an employee, the right is determined by the law of the State in which the employee is mainly employed (or, if indeterminate, the State where the employer has a place of business to which the employee is attached).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 7(1) — For proceedings before the Eurasian Office the applicant is deemed entitled (Article 7(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of priority
rubrics_metrics.description: The right of priority shall be recognized in conformity with the Paris Convention for the Protection of Industrial Property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 8 — Claiming priority must follow Paris Convention rules; Patent Regulations provide detail on claiming of priority (Article 19(v)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extent of legal protection determined by claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent of the legal protection conferred by a Eurasian patent shall be determined by the claims; the description and drawings shall serve only to interpret the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 10 — Interpretation guidance and claim-related rules are addressed in Patent Regulations (Article 14(vii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of Eurasian patent
rubrics_metrics.description: The term of a Eurasian patent shall be 20 years from the filing date of the Eurasian application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 11 — Standard 20-year term from filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision for provisional protection after publication
rubrics_metrics.description: After an application has been published, the applicant shall enjoy provisional protection in conformity with the national legislation of the Contracting States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 9(3) — Provisional protection mechanics depend on each Contracting State's law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory licenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Compulsory licenses for the use of a Eurasian patent by third parties may be granted in conformity with the Paris Convention by the competent authority of a Contracting State with effect in the territory of that State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 12(1) — Decisions granting compulsory licenses may be contested in the courts or other competent authorities of that Contracting State (Article 12(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolution of validity and infringement disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: Any dispute arising from the validity or the infringement of a Eurasian patent in a given Contracting State shall be resolved by the national courts or other competent authorities of that State on the basis of this Convention and the Patent Regulations; the decision has effect only in the territory of that Contracting State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 13(1) — National courts must apply the Convention and Patent Regulations; they may require translations (Article 13(3)); Contracting States must provide same civil or other liability as for national patents (Article 13(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Regulations: definition of criteria of patentability and disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent Regulations shall provide for the definition of the criteria of patentability (including novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability) and the requirement of the disclosure of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 14(i) — Patent Regulations will elaborate definitions and tests for these core concepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Regulations: disclosures that do not affect patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent Regulations shall specify disclosures that do not affect the patentability of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 14(ii) — Examples and conditions for non-prejudicial disclosures to be set in Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Regulations: unity of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent Regulations shall provide for the requirement of unity of invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 14(iii) — Unity tests and consequences for lack of unity are to be set out in Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Regulations: definition and effects of the right of priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent Regulations shall define the right of priority and its effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 14(iv) — Details on claiming priority and effect on filing/novelty to be prescribed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Regulations: definition of exclusive right
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent Regulations shall define the exclusive right in the patented invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 14(v) — Scope and limitations of exclusive rights to be regulated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Regulations: right of the prior user
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent Regulations shall provide for the right of the prior user.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 14(vi) — Prior user rights and conditions will be defined in Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Regulations: interpretation of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent Regulations shall provide for the interpretation of the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 14(vii) — Rules for interpreting claim language, role of description/drawings to be set out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Regulations: inventor’s right to be mentioned
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent Regulations shall provide for the right of the inventor to be mentioned in the Eurasian application and Eurasian patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 14(viii) — Procedures and remedies regarding attribution to be detailed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Regulations: assignment and transfer of rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent Regulations shall provide for the assignment and other transfer of the right to a Eurasian application or patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 14(ix) — Formalities for assignment and recording transfers will be prescribed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Regulations: confidentiality in processing applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent Regulations shall provide for confidentiality in processing Eurasian applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 14(x) — Confidentiality obligations for Office and staff to be set out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to file a Eurasian application (filing route)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Eurasian application may be filed with the Eurasian Office or, for applicants from a Contracting State where provided by national law, filed through the national Patent Office, which shall transmit it to the Eurasian Office within prescribed time limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 15(1)-(2) — Filing through a national Office requires the national Office to verify form compliance; transmission deadlines and fee payments differ by route.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees on filing, search, publication and other processing (unitary procedural fee)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Eurasian application is filed with the Eurasian Office, a unitary procedural fee for filing, search, publication and other processing shall be payable to that Office at the time of filing; when filed through a national Office, a fee for examination as to form is payable to the national Office at filing and the unitary procedural fee to the Eurasian Office upon transmittal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 15(2) and Article 18(1) — Fee timing depends on filing route; Patent Regulations and Admin Council will set amounts and currencies (Article 19(vi), Article 18(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination as to form and search by the Eurasian Office
rubrics_metrics.description: The Eurasian Office shall verify compliance of the Eurasian application with requirements as to form and shall carry out a search which shall result in a search report forwarded to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 15(3) — National Offices perform form examination when filing through them; searches follow and produce a search report (see publication timing Article 15(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication timing and early publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The Eurasian Office shall publish the Eurasian application together with the search report promptly after expiry of 18 months from the filing date or priority date; at applicant's request earlier publication is possible, in which case the search report will be published separately as soon as available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 15(4) — Applicants may request early publication; search report handling described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for substantive examination and time limit
rubrics_metrics.description: At the applicant's request filed with the Eurasian Office before the expiry of six months from the date of publication of the search report, the Eurasian Office shall carry out substantive examination of the Eurasian application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 15(5)-(6) — The request is subject to payment of an examination fee (Article 15(6)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-making collegia composition and grant/rejection procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision to grant or reject shall be made by collegia composed of three examiners who shall be staff members of the Eurasian Office and, unless otherwise decided, nationals of different Contracting States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 15(7) — Collegia composition rules; Administrative Council may change nationality requirement by unanimous decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal against refusal and appeal collegium composition
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant disagrees with a refusal, he may within three months lodge an appeal to be examined by a collegium composed in conformity with collegium rules; the collegium shall include at least two examiners who did not participate in the initial decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 15(8)-(9) — Appeal lodging is subject to payment of a fee; time limit is three months from receipt of notice of refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant conditioned on payment of grant fee
rubrics_metrics.description: The grant of a Eurasian patent is subject to payment of a fee to the Eurasian Office within three months after the applicant receives notice that the Office is ready to grant the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 15(10) — Payment deadline and effect tied to receipt of notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of grant across Contracting States and designation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to Article 17, a Eurasian patent shall have effect on the territory of all Contracting States from the date of its publication; continuation of effect in each Contracting State requires designation of that State and payment of maintenance fees (see Article 17).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 15(11) and Article 17(3) — Designation by name is required for continued effect in each State; maintenance fee and designation timing linked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation before the Eurasian Office and patent agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person entitled to be a representative before a national Office and registered with the Eurasian Office as a patent agent may act as representative before the Eurasian Office; applicants without residence or principal place of business in any Contracting State must be represented by such a patent agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 15(12) — Patent agent registration and national qualifications matter; persons resident in a Contracting State may act personally or through agents or representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of Eurasian applications into national applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Before expiry of six months from receipt of notice of refusal (or refusal to allow an appeal), applicant may request designation of Contracting States where he wishes to obtain national patents; the Eurasian application shall be treated in those States as a regular national application with the filing and priority date of the Eurasian application, processed by the national Office upon payment of national fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 16(1)-(2) — Conversion preserves filing/priority dates and triggers national processing and fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance fees and yearly payment schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintenance of a Eurasian patent is subject to annual payment of fees payable in each of the years following grant by the date corresponding to the filing date of the Eurasian application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 17(1)-(2) — Timing corresponds to filing date each year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation and fee per Contracting State for continued effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuing effect of a Eurasian patent in each Contracting State requires the owner to designate by name each Contracting State in which he wishes the effect to continue; designation is addressed to the Eurasian Office and made at the same time as the maintenance fee, payable in respect of each designated Contracting State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 17(3) — Designation and fee are per-State; failure to designate will stop effect in that State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment and distribution of fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees concerning any Eurasian application or patent and charges for services shall be payable to the Eurasian Office and, subject to Article 18(2), belong to the Organization; maintenance fees payable to the Eurasian Office shall be distributed between the Organization and designated Contracting States per a ratio fixed by Administrative Council, with at least one-fifth of each designation fee belonging to the Organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 18(1)-(2) — National Offices receive the form-examination/transmittal fee when filed through them (Article 15(2)); Admin Council fixes distribution and amount (two-thirds majority for some decisions per Article 3(3)(vii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Regulations: procedural provisions to be provided
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Regulations shall provide details concerning Eurasian patent procedure, including requirements as to form and contents of the application; requirements for patent agents and their certification/registration; filing date; calculation of time limits; claiming priority; currencies and fee procedures; amendment/correction of the application; patent search and examination; documentation and information services; publication; Register and Gazette; administrative revocation conditions and procedures; conversion into national applications; rules where multiple inventors/applicants/owners/representatives exist; and contacts and procedure for consultation of Office files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 19(i)-(xvi) — The Regulations will contain the detailed procedural rules for all listed items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of the Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Cooperation Treaty and its Regulations shall be applied in the Eurasian Patent System and shall prevail in case of conflict between them and this Convention and its Regulations; the Eurasian Office shall be a receiving Office and a designated and elected Office, and may with authorization apply for status as an International Searching and Preliminary Examining Authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 20 — PCT norms integrated; applicants can use PCT procedures; PCT prevails on conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional search agreements with national/regional offices
rubrics_metrics.description: The Eurasian Office may, with Administrative Council authorization, conclude agreements with national or regional patent offices for carrying out searches in relation to Eurasian applications, provided those offices can carry out searches of the same type as those under the PCT in all or selected fields of technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 21(1) — Transitional practical arrangements for search capacities; ensures quality comparable to PCT searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of national examiners in collegia during transition
rubrics_metrics.description: During transitional periods collegia of three examiners may consist of examiners recommended by national Offices of the Contracting States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 21(2) — Temporary composition flexibility to allow participation of national examiners in collegia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence of national patent systems retained
rubrics_metrics.description: This Convention shall not prejudice the right of any Contracting State to grant national patents nor prevent any Contracting State from participating on its own in international organizations or other cooperation in the field of industrial property protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 22(1)-(2) — Eurasian system coexists with national patent rights and other international activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination of patent information
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Contracting State shall receive, free of charge, the Gazette of the Eurasian Office and the descriptions of Eurasian applications and patents; no publication of the Eurasian Office may be disseminated free of charge without the authorization of the Administrative Council (subject to paragraph (1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 25(1)-(2) — Information access provisions and Administrative Council control over further free dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry into force, accession, and no reservations permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Any State that is a UN member and bound by the Paris Convention and the PCT may become party by signing and ratifying or acceding; no reservations to the Convention are permitted; entry into force timing specified (three months after third ratification for first three States, otherwise three months after ratification/accession).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 26(2)-(4) — Procedural requirements for States to join and timing of entry into force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denunciation and depositary
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Contracting State may denounce the Convention by notification to the Director General of WIPO, taking effect six months after receipt; the Director General of WIPO is the depositary of the Convention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles 27-28 — Formal denunciation mechanics and WIPO's depositary role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Council composition, quorum, voting and powers
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Contracting State is represented in the Administrative Council with one vote; two-thirds of the Contracting States constitute a quorum; decisions by consensus or simple majority unless unanimity or a two-thirds majority is required; Administrative Council adopts Rules of Procedure and, by two-thirds majority, the Patent Regulations, Financial Regulations and Administrative Regulations and establishes annual budget by two-thirds majority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 3(1)-(3) — Governance and decision-making rules for the Organization; Administrative Council also appoints/elects key officials and approves agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eurasian Office structure, President and staff quotas
rubrics_metrics.description: The Eurasian Office is headed by a President who determines structure and appoints staff; each Contracting State shall have a quota in respect of the staff determined in the Administrative Regulations; Office located in Moscow and official language is Russian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 2(3)-(6) and Article 4 — Organizational and headquarters provisions; privileges and immunities described (Article 2(7)).
